Candidate launch is held behind a same-process pre-exec pipe guard: candidate pidfd and PID record are established first; the watchdog must open its own pidfd to that still-inert guard and acknowledge ready supervision before the parent may release the guard. Any pidfd/PID-record/watchdog/ready setup failure closes the guard without starting llama. Both start-failure recovery and standalone cleanup treat the acknowledged pre-exec guard and reviewed llama identity as the same owned task; cleanup is pidfd-only, recovery PID/watchdog metadata is retained until owned-process exit plus listener absence are actually proved, and only then may supervision/recovery metadata be released. No numeric PID/PGID signaling is allowed.
